country.comment: The six-dimension water and sanitation affordability framework is empirically applied to Brazil as a national case study.
country.where_found: PDF p. 4, Abstract; PDF p. 9, Section 3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Most state-level distributions are presented graphically in maps and bar charts (Figures 1-10 and Appendices A-B) without regression estimates, confidence intervals, or p-values; all exact printed text and caption figures are reported above.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive cross-sectional indicator analysis (no regression point estimates, 95% CIs, or p-values reported): across 4,052 Brazilian municipalities, WSS coverage within state-utility service areas ranges from 96.5% water supply and 89.6% sanitation in São Paulo (SABESP; and 99.0% water / 91.8% sanitation in Distrito Federal) down to 34.9% water supply and 3.1% sanitation in Rondônia (and 31% water / 2% sanitation in Alagoas). At a 5% income threshold, conventional state-average-wage affordability ratios (AR1) appear affordable in most states (exceeding 5% mainly in Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, and Ceará), masking severe affordability burdens for poorer households (earning <= 1/2 minimum wage) without social tariffs (AR3) and near-poor households at 60% of average wage excluded from social tariffs (AR4) (e.g., in Cuiabá, poorer-household AR is 7.1% without social tariffs vs. 4.8% with social tariffs, and 5.2% at 60% of average wage). Social tariff enrollment reaches at most 41.2% of eligible low-income families (in Minas Gerais, the highest-access state; COSAMA in Amazonas offers no social tariff), and one-time water and wastewater connection fees exceed 40% of monthly household income for poorer families in several states (30.5% in Cuiabá).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 16-21, Sections 3.3.1-3.3.6 and Figures 1-10; PDF pp. 26-30, Appendices A-B

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <= 2 by cross-sectional observational design; rated 1 because the study computes descriptive cross-sectional affordability and coverage ratios from aggregated secondary datasets and published tariff/connection-fee schedules (comparing state CADÚnico low-income counts with SNIS social-tariff connection counts) without directly observing household-level administrative screening, enrollment barriers, or connection refusals (citing prior literature for restricted local rules and lack of information).

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines regular tariffs and one-time upfront water/wastewater connection fees (BURDEN: fees), utility social tariff discounts and reduced connection fees for vulnerable families alongside low social-tariff reach (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: hardship_exception, accommodation), utility service-area boundaries and CADÚnico/income eligibility cutoffs excluding near-poor households (ELIGIBILITY: service_area), and decentralized tariff/subsidy regulation across >90 subnational regulators, municipalities, and state utilities (institutional_fragmentation).
